pairs.subject: sync-replication
pairs.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:31 The v1→ledger projection runs only when the operator CLI runs it or when a ledger-showing page calls freshLedger(). The periodic tick that change-tracking-and-cursors requires as a floor was rejected on purpose, so the ledger can stay stale for as long as nobody renders a page; no data is lost, because every sync re-reads everything, but how long the latency can grow has no bound.

techniques.evidence: lib/ledger/v1/types.ts:12 Declared one-way mirror: v1 stores are the authority and the ledger never writes back. The stream set is one registry (sources.ts V1_SOURCES), and the engine iterates it generically.

lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:31 No cursor: each sync is a full re-read appended idempotently by key, so nothing is skipped. Read-time wakes are the only automatic cadence, and the tick floor was deliberately rejected, so staleness is unbounded when nothing reads. Batched backfill (BATCH=200) and the separate read/project/append failure classes do conform.

lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:138 Key collisions are compared by canonical content (kernel ingest identity()), never by clock. An existing key with the same content is counted as 'existing'; one with different content is counted as 'drifted' and reported. The append-only policy (the held event stands) is the authority-wins rule of a one-way mirror.

lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:167 Each source gets its own health row (last_ok_at, fail_streak, last_error verbatim in kernel ingest_sources). readOne turns any throw into a classed per-source failure, so one source's failure strands no other. reconcile() compares the source tally with the ledger count.

lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:206 The replica is an append-only event ledger of facts, not a mirror of records. History the source has since dropped stays in the ledger by design, and the live view is read from v1 at render time, so a removed v1 record cannot resurrect anything.
lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:133 There is no client outbox and no socket push. Batches are local SQLite transactions in the same process, so there is no in-flight state to keep per connection.

pairs.registryProposal: change-tracking-and-cursors requires a periodic tick as the floor. It does not cover a read-triggered projection whose only readers are page renders, where an idle system has nobody to be stale for. The technique could state whether a read-on-demand freshness check counts as the floor when every read path calls it. Here one read path (the agents' API) does not.
